slides.title: The road, in one minute
slides.text: Fast recap, because this band moves quickly. Messages travel as numbered packets, routers pass them hop by hop, and a protocol is the shared rules every stop follows.
slides.alt: Rules of the Road opens: numbered packets wait at the first router, ready to travel by the shared rules.

slides.title: Got it, and spot the gap
slides.text: The receiver says got it for each packet. A missing number is asked for again, and extra copies are thrown away.
slides.alt: The delivery is under way: packets have been sent and the receiver is saying got it, watching for a gap.

slides.title: Three things on an open road
slides.text: Unsealed, a packet is a postcard on an open road. An interceptor can read it, copy it and keep the copy, or change its words before it travels on.

slides.title: A count catches accidents
slides.text: A checksum catches packets damaged by accident, when the count no longer matches. An enemy who changes a packet can fix the count too, so integrity needs more than a count.
slides.alt: A later protocol level on the road: here a damaged packet must be spotted by its count and sent again.

slides.title: Roads you do not control
slides.text: Every network you do not control is part of the threat surface. This unit asks one question: what closes each hole? Sealing comes next, and copies after that.

words.means: shared rules computers follow to talk
arriving unchanged, exactly as the sender sent it
to stop and catch something while it is on its way
the places where a packet can be reached while it travels

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Packet Post at Rules of the Road and finish 4 levels. Each time a packet is resent, say why: missing, or damaged?
slides.alt: A second protocol level: every router on the road follows the same rules, or no packet could be passed on.
